title: Analyzing Polarization in Social Media: Method and Application to Tweets on 21 Mass Shootings
reasoning: The paper is a sociolinguistic analysis of political polarization on Twitter following mass shooting events. While the research categorizes certain linguistic tokens related to religious identity (e.g., 'Islamist', 'Christian') and religious expressions (e.g., 'prayer') within its topic modeling and affect analysis, it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, faith, morals, or ethics themselves.
